content: 1. Darunavir increases the concentration or effect of indinavir by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Both darunavir and indinavir elevate the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. 2. Indinavir increases the concentration or effect of cobicistat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 3. Cobicistat increases the concentration or effect of infigratinib by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir also increases the concentration or effect of infigratinib through the same mechanism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 4. Darunavir reduces the efficacy of insulin aspart due to insulin resistance caused by protease inhibitors. Monitor closely for hyperglycemia. 5. Darunavir reduces the efficacy of insulin degludec through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. HIV protease inhibitors may induce new-onset diabetes mellitus, worsen existing diabetes, or cause hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. 6. Darunavir reduces the efficacy of insulin detemir, insulin glargine, insulin glulisine, and inhaled insulin through mechanisms related to insulin resistance or pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely for hyperglycemia. 7. Darunavir reduces the efficacy of insulin lispro, insulin NPH, and regular human insulin due to insulin resistance. Use caution and monitor closely for hyperglycemia. 8. Cobicistat increases the concentration or effect of irinotecan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated, especially when coadministered with atazanavir. 9. Darunavir increases the concentration or effect of irinotecan and irinotecan liposomal by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 10. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the concentration or effect of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 11. Isoniazid increases the concentration or effect of cobicistat and darunavir by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Cobicistat increases the concentration or effect of isradipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir also increases isradipine levels, but the clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 13. Darunavir increases the concentration or effect of istradefylline by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Istradefylline increases CYP3A4 substrate levels at higher doses (40 mg/day) but not at lower doses (20 mg/day). 14. Cobicistat increases the concentration or effect of itraconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Darunavir also interacts with itraconazole, increasing its effects. 15. Darunavir increases the concentration or effect of ivabradine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Cobicistat also increases ivabradine levels, and coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 16. Cobicistat and darunavir increase the concentration or effect of ivacaftor by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the ivacaftor dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to specific product guidelines for dosage adjustments. 17. Cobicistat increases the concentration or effect of ivosidenib by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily if unavoidable. If the inhibitor is discontinued, increase the ivosidenib dose to the recommended 500 mg daily after at least five half-lives of the inhibitor. 18. Darunavir increases the concentration or effect of ivosidenib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or replace with alternative therapies. 19. Darunavir increases the concentration or effect of ixabepilone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use alternative drugs. Cobicistat also increases ixabepilone levels, and coadministration should be avoided. 20. Darunavir and cobicistat have minor or unknown significance in their interaction with ixazomib. Clinical trials indicate no meaningful change in ixazomib exposure when coadministered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 21. Darunavir decreases the concentration or effect of ketamine by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Cobicistat and ketoconazole increase each other's levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Darunavir also interacts with ketoconazole, increasing its effects. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 23. Darunavir increases the concentration or effect of lacosamide by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider reducing the lacosamide dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 24. Cobicistat increases the concentration or effect of lansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the concentration or effect of lapatinib by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, adjust the lapatinib dose to 500 mg daily and increase to the indicated dose once cobicistat is discontinued. 26. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the concentration or effect of larotrectinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 27. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the concentration or effect of lefamulin by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 28. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the concentration or effect of lemborexant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 29. Lenacapavir increases the concentration or effect of darunavir and cobicistat by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase the risk of adverse reactions to CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose. 30. Darunavir and cobicistat increase the concentration or effect of leniolisib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 31. Letermovir increases darunavir levels by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat increases letermovir levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Cobicistat and darunavir increase the concentration or effect of levamlodipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Coadministration with CYP3A inhibitors may require dose reduction of amlodipine. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema. 33. Cobicistat and levoketoconazole increase each other's levels by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Darunavir also interacts with levoketoconazole, increasing its effects. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 34. Darunavir increases the concentration or effect of levomilnacipran by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed 80 mg/day of levomilnacipran when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Cobicistat also increases levomilnacipran levels, and alternative drugs should be considered.
